        "body": "If you nested a `Router` at `/` the path for the final routes would start with a double slash.\r\n\r\nFixes https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/issues/690\r\n\r\nAside about how nesting works:\r\n\r\nWhen you nest a service we try and downcast it to a `Router`. If that succeeds we simply move all the paths from one router onto another, with the path prefix added plus a middleware that strips the prefix before calling the `MethodRouter`. That simplifies lots of things internally because there is only one router that has all the paths. It also improves performance since matchit can see the entire tree. part.text:
Fixed the issue in `axum/src/routing/mod.rs`:

- `nest("")` no longer panics; it's normalized to mean the same as `nest("/")` (axum/src/routing/mod.rs:169-173).
- When joining a nested `Router`'s paths with the nest prefix, a `/` prefix is no longer concatenated onto nested paths (which produced `//foo` and `GET / -> 404`); the nested path is used as-is when the prefix is `/` (axum/src/routing/mod.rs:211-220).

Verified: `cargo test -p axum --lib` passes with all 125 tests, including `nesting_router_at_root`, `nesting_router_at_empty_path`, and `nesting_handler_at_root`.
